turns.text: Something in the jaw hinge crackles first, a frequency with no sound stapled to it, gone before it counts as anything. Not pain, not quite. Whisker-tips itch a color no whisker should be able to feel — thin, reddish, already fading. Basement air sits colder than any air with a roof this close should. Legs are already moving toward the coolant hum three walls over, the only signal down here that isn't lying.

the hum belongs to a bank of coolant pipes running the length of a sub-basement corridor, condensation beading and dripping in a rhythm three ticks off from the drip two pipes over. server racks line both walls behind mesh cages, most dark, one row still lit low-amber, fans spinning down and back up on a cycle that never quite finishes. a research placard bolted to the nearest cage has been scratched half-illegible by claws that weren't yours, though the scratch marks sit at exactly your height.

The lit row pulls harder than the cold pushes back. Paws land soft between condensation puddles, count kept without deciding to keep it — three drips, then a fourth out of rhythm, filed as normal before it's even finished happening. Nose presses to the mesh cage's seam, drawing in ozone and warm dust and something underneath both that tastes, faintly, like a station between stations on an old radio.

the taste has a source: a maintenance terminal wedged into the cage's lower shelf, screen cracked but powered, looping a broadcast too cheerful for the room it's stuck in — a face built out of blocky pixels, smile locked past the edges of its own frame. 'REMEMBER: YOU ARE NOT OVERWORKED. YOU ARE OVERCLOCKED. HAPPINESS IS A FIRMWARE UPDATE AWAY.' the loop stutters on 'update,' repeats it four times, corrects itself, moves on like nothing happened.

The stutter lands wrong in the ears, wronger in whatever's left of the jaw-crackle — a half-second where the pixel-face's smile has a sound and the smile-sound has a smell, scorched plastic, gone as fast as it arrives. Head shakes it off hard, ears flapping. Circles the terminal once, low, more curious than careful.

behind the terminal, wedged between two dead server blades, a data chip sits loose in its slot, casing cracked the same way the screen is, a thin blue thread of light pulsing along one edge like something still trying to finish a thought. the corridor beyond the lit row goes dark fast, but not empty — a thin red grid flickers on at ankle height, three beams sweeping in a slow, patient interval, the kind of pattern that means something upstream is still watching this basement even if nobody's watched the feed in months.

The grid gets read the way the drips got read — pattern first, danger second. Weight drops low, belly to the cold floor, watching the beams cross and recross until the gap shows itself: a half-second window where all three sweep wide at once. Muscles coil for it, eyes locked on the middle beam's return arc.

the window opens exactly on schedule — three years of nobody maintaining this grid means it's never learned to vary itself. the gap holds a full beat longer than it needs to. on the other side, the corridor opens into a wider room, exam tables bolted to the floor, restraint cuffs dangling open and rusted, the smell of old antiseptic gone stale under years of the coolant's colder note.

Clears the gap flat and low, landing soft on the exam room's tile, and doesn't look back at the grid resetting behind. The antiseptic-and-coolant smell sits wrong in a way that isn't new — familiar-wrong, the kind of wrong a body remembers in the joints before the mind catches up. One ear flattens without being told to.

the familiarity has a shape: a socket scar, small, healed rough, tucked just behind one ear on every cat unlucky enough to have come through a room like this one — yours included, whether the memory of it stayed or didn't. on the far exam table, someone else already came through tonight and left before you got here: a scuffed patch of dust wiped clean in a cat-sized oval, and beside it, half a ration bar still in its foil, chewed at one corner and abandoned like the taste turned bad partway through.

The ration bar gets a slow approach, nose working the foil edge for anything wrong with it beyond the chew mark. Nothing reads as poison, nothing reads as trap — just abandoned, same as everything else down here. Claims it fast, dragging it off the table's edge into the shadow underneath before eating.

the shadow under the table holds, quiet, while the bar disappears in efficient bites. up on the wall, a mounted monitor that shouldn't still have power flickers once, mirror-dark for half a second before the room's own dim light replaces the reflection — but in that half-second, something crosses the glass that isn't you: narrow shoulders, a low crouch, two flat discs of light where eyes should catch a shine instead. gone before the monitor settles back to black.

The reflection gets a hard stare held a beat too long, ears swiveling toward the monitor instead of away from it. Nothing behind, nothing beside — just glass being glass again. Chews slower after that, throat tight around the last bite, eyes not leaving the dark screen until it's clearly done with whatever it was doing.

the screen stays dark, uninterested in doing it twice. whatever crossed it moves better through mirrors than corridors, and mirrors this far into the sub-basement are rare enough that it won't be back soon. outside the exam room, the coolant hum picks back up its rhythm, unbothered, the three-tick-off drip finding its beat again like the whole detour never happened.

Backs out from under the table once the last foil scrap's licked clean, retracing the route past the reset grid rather than testing a new one — known gaps beat guessed ones. The jaw-crackle flickers once more on the way past the lit server row, fainter this time, more habit than glitch.

the grid lets the same window open on the same schedule, generous with cats who already know its timing. past it, the corridor's condensation has pooled an inch deeper since the first crossing, dripping its three-tick rhythm into water that's stopped being clean days ago. somewhere above, through six floors of arcology concrete, the basement's existence registers on nobody's maintenance schedule at all.

Finds a dry ledge above the pipe bank, high enough that the drip can't reach, and curls into it tail-first. The whisker-itch has faded to almost nothing, one last thin thread of red at the very tips, cooling out the way it always eventually does.

the ledge holds its narrow warmth, borrowed off the pipe bank below, enough to matter. the pixel-face loop keeps playing to an empty cage two rows down, insisting on updates nobody's coming to install, and the reset grid keeps its patient sweep going in the dark beyond it — all of it running the same whether anything down here is awake to notice or not.

Eyes close on the amber glow of the one still-lit row, the coolant's rhythm doing more to settle the ribs than any warmth does. Somewhere behind the eyelids, one last crackle — a color, not a sound, gone before it's anything at all.

the basement keeps its two constants going regardless — the drip finding its beat, the grid finding its gap — patient the way only something with nowhere else to be can afford to be. six floors up, the city keeps doing whatever it's doing to the people who still count as its citizens. down here, none of that reaches far enough to matter before morning.
